q: 遇到没深用过的技术，怎么诚实又不掉价地开口？
q_en: Facing tech you haven't used deeply, how do you speak honestly without losing credibility?
options: Exactly-once, um, exactly-once semantics... okay, so, let me, let me think how Kafka...
I haven't used exactly-once directly, but from first principles I'd expect idempotent writes plus committing offsets in one transaction.
Oh yeah, exactly-once just means Kafka literally never sends any message twice, so it's fully guaranteed out of the box, nothing to configure.
Honestly I've never touched that part, so I really don't know — sorry, maybe we can just skip this one.
tradeoff: 认领边界+推原理 vs 硬编一个确定答案：承认没用过换来可信的推理，代价是显得不熟；硬编听着自信却可能整段错。
why: 没深用过就先认领边界「I haven't used X directly」，再用「from first principles」把已知原理推出来，比卡死或硬编都可信。
why_en: Name the boundary — "I haven't used X directly" — then reason from first principles, which reads far stronger than freezing or bluffing.
whenOtherWins: 只有当你确实深用过、能直接讲实现时，才跳过「没用过」的免责，直接给答案更有分量。

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka：一个分布式消息/事件流平台。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed messaging and event-streaming platform.

termDefinitions.meaning: exactly-once：每条消息在处理结果上不重不漏、恰好生效一次的语义。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exactly-once means each message takes effect once — never lost, never duplicated.

termDefinitions.meaning: 幂等：同一操作执行一次或多次，结果相同。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotent means running the same operation once or many times yields the same result.

termDefinitions.meaning: offset：消费者在 Kafka 分区中读到的位置游标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An offset is the position cursor tracking how far a consumer has read in a Kafka partition.

scenario_en: In an Alterion coding round you have a brute-force solution but you're stuck on optimizing, mind blank — last time you froze on "okay... okay..." for half a minute.
q: 彻底卡住、需要提示时，怎么开口既不慌又不放弃？
q_en: Truly stuck and needing a hint — how do you speak up without panicking or quitting?
options: I've got a working brute force but I'm stuck making it faster — can I get a hint on which direction to explore?
Okay... okay, so... um, faster, faster, how to make it faster, let me, let me think...
It's already optimal, this brute force is basically O(n), so I don't think we can really do better here.
Yeah I'm really stuck, I honestly don't think I can figure this one out — sorry, I guess this just isn't my strongest area.
tradeoff: 主动要定向提示 vs 硬撑或弃题：求助换来推进和协作感，代价是暴露卡点；硬撑或放弃只会让空白更久。
why: 彻底卡住时，主动「can I get a hint on...?」把求助变成缩小范围的推进，比僵在「okay...」或硬说已最优都体面。
why_en: When truly stuck, ask "can I get a hint on X?" — a scoped ask moves you forward, unlike freezing on "okay..." or bluffing "it's optimal."
whenOtherWins: 只有当你其实还有没试的思路时，先自己出声试一版，再决定要不要要提示。

scenario: Convoke 面，面试官问你刚写的函数时间复杂度。你不确定，上次脱口「O(n) 吧」被追问就崩了。

q_en: Unsure of the complexity — how do you speak without wild-guessing or faking it?
options: It's O(n), definitely — there's just one main loop, so it's linear, I'm pretty sure.
Complexity, um, the complexity is... okay, so, the loop, the loop runs, let me, let me think...
Honestly I'm not great at complexity analysis, so I'd rather not just guess and get it wrong — sorry about that.
Let me reason through it — a loop inside a loop, so it's n times n, which is O(n²).
tradeoff: 出声逐步推导 vs 直接抛一个数字：推导换来可验证的可信度，代价是慢一点；直接报数字快却可能自信地错。
why: 没把握时说「let me reason through it」，把外层×内层一步步推出来，好过乱猜一个数字或直接说不擅长。
why_en: When unsure, say "let me reason through it" and walk the outer×inner loops step by step — better than a wild guess or "I'm not good at this."
whenOtherWins: 只有当复杂度一眼可见、你完全确定时，才直接报结果，不必先声明「让我推一下」。

tradeoff: 分清已知与盲区 vs 硬编完整答案：坦白哪块模糊换来可信度，代价是暴露短板；硬编全懂一被追问就崩。
why: 只懂一半就说清「I know X, but the exact Y I'm fuzzy on」，把确定和不确定分开，比硬编全懂或直接弃答都可信。
why_en: When you half-know it, separate the two — "I know X, but the exact Y I'm fuzzy on" — more credible than faking full mastery or skipping it.
whenOtherWins: 只有当你其实完全掌握时，才别自贬「fuzzy」，直接讲清结构更有说服力。
options_en: Index, um, how does index, the index, okay, so it makes it faster, faster, let me, let me think...
I know an index gives faster lookups — the exact structure I'm fuzzy on, but I believe it's a B-tree.
Sure, an index is a full copy of the table sorted differently, so every query just reads that copy instead.
I only kind of know how indexes work, so I'd probably get the details wrong — maybe skip this one, sorry.
optionMeanings: 复读「index, um」卡在「let me think」。
先讲确定的（加速查找），再标出模糊处（结构）。
自信断言索引是整表的排序副本（错）。
以「只懂一半」为由请求跳过。
optionMeanings_en: Echoes 'index, um,' stalls on 'let me think.'
States the known part (faster lookups), flags the fuzzy part.
Confidently claims an index is a sorted full copy (wrong).
Asks to skip, citing 'only half-know it.'
optionScenarioImpacts: 卡壳念出声，显得基础虚。
已知部分立住，坦白反而显得可信。
自信但错误，一追问结构就穿帮。
主动弃答，错失展示已知的机会。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Voiced stall — fundamentals look shaky.
The known part lands; the honesty reads as credible.
Confident but wrong; a structure probe exposes it.
Self-skips, wasting a chance to show what you know.
optionDirectness: 错在冻结复读，把停顿念出声。
抓住「分清已知与盲区」的诚实起手。
错在硬编一个自信的错误答案。
错在因半懂就整段弃答。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong — frozen echo, voicing the pause.
Nails it: separate what you know from the fuzzy part.
Wrong — bluffs a confident, wrong answer.
Wrong — skips entirely over half-knowing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引：为加速查询而额外维护的数据结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An index is an extra data structure maintained to speed up queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: B-tree（B 树）：数据库常用的平衡多叉树索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree is a balanced multi-way tree commonly used as a database index structure.

termDefinitions.meaning: lookup（查找）：按 key 定位到对应数据的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lookup is the operation of locating data by its key.

scenario: WOP 支付面，面试官问一个你没算过的估算题（比如某功能每天大概多少写入）。上次直接「I don't know the number」就没了。
scenario_en: In a WOP payments round the interviewer asks an estimation you've never done (say, roughly how many writes a feature gets per day). Last time you just said "I don't know the number" and stopped.
q: 碰到没算过的估算题，怎么开口把它推出来？
q_en: Facing an estimation you've never done — how do you open and reason it out?
options: I don't really know the exact number, and I've never measured it, so I couldn't give you a figure here, sorry.
It's about a million writes a day, definitely around a million, that's just the typical number for this.
I don't have the number, but let me reason through it — start from daily users, then writes per user.
Writes, um, writes per day, okay, so how many, how many writes, let me, let me think about writes...
tradeoff: 从假设逐步推算 vs 抛一个记住的数字：推导换来可检验的估算，代价是慢；直接抛数字快却可能凭空捏造。
why: 没算过的估算题别停在「I don't know the number」，改说「let me reason through it」，从用户量×人均写入一步步推，好过硬编数字或放弃。
why_en: For an unfamiliar estimate, don't stop at "I don't know the number" — say "let me reason through it" and build from users × writes-per-user, better than inventing a figure or quitting.
whenOtherWins: 只有当你手上正好有真实数字、能直接引用时，才跳过推导，直接给数据更有力。
options_en: I don't really know the exact number, and I've never measured it, so I couldn't give you a figure here, sorry.
It's about a million writes a day, definitely around a million, that's just the typical number for this.
I don't have the number, but let me reason through it — start from daily users, then writes per user.
Writes, um, writes per day, okay, so how many, how many writes, let me, let me think about writes...
optionMeanings: 以「没测过」为由拒绝给任何估算。
凭空断言「大约一百万」，当成典型值（捏造）。
承认没数字，但从用户量×人均写入逐步推。
复读「writes, um」卡在「let me think」。
optionMeanings_en: Refuses any estimate, citing 'never measured it.'
Invents 'about a million,' passing it as typical (fabricated).
Admits no number, builds from users × writes-per-user.
Echoes 'writes, um,' stalls on 'let me think.'
optionScenarioImpacts: 直接放弃，错失估算能力的展示。
凭空数字，一问依据就崩。
推导可被检验，显示结构化思维。
卡壳念出声，显得没方向。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Quits outright, wasting an estimation signal.
A made-up figure collapses when its basis is asked.
Verifiable derivation — shows structured thinking.
Voiced stall — reads as directionless.
optionDirectness: 错在直接弃答不推导。
错在凭空捏造一个自信的数字。
抓住「从假设逐步推算」的稳健起手。
错在冻结复读，把停顿念出声。

Wrong — fabricates a confident number.

Wrong — frozen echo, voicing the pause.
